the island where Neoptolemus was brought up (Iliad 19.326–327)

510.n: ἦ τοι (= ἤτοι), answered by αὐτὰρ ὅτʼ (513), like μέν … δέ
= ὅτε, with the iterative optative φραζοίμεθα (Merry on 11.510)

in apposition: πόλιν Τροίην 'the city Troy', like πόλιν Καλυδῶνα Iliad 9.530; some ancient readers, Aristarchus among them, took it as a trisyllabic adjective, needlessly in Merry's view (Merry on 11.510 and critical note)
iterative optative after ὅτε, of repeated past action; middle 'consider, plan': φράζεσθαι βουλάς 'take counsel'

511.n: + gen.: he did not miss the right words, did not say the wrong ones, cf. ἀφαμαρτοεπής Iliad 3.215 (Merry on 11.511)

512.n: iter. (-σκ-), unaugmented: 'used to outdo (him)', 'Nestor and I alone were his masters' in speaking (Merry on 11.511); only here in Homer; the scholia record a second reading νεικέσκομεν, from νεικέω (Merry's critical note on 11.512)
dual 'we two alone', with the plural verb

513.n: iterative optative; most manuscripts have μαρνοίμεθʼ, Bekker's μαρναίμεθα rests on one (Merry's critical note on 11.513)
instrumental dative; La Roche reads Ἀχαιοί with almost all manuscripts (Merry's critical note on 11.513)

514.n: οὔ ποτε 'never'; accent from enclitic ποτʼ; οὔ ποτʼ ἐνὶ πληθυῖ μένεν ἀνδρῶν as Iliad 22.458, of Hector
more than πληθύς: the thick of the fight, as Iliad 5.353 (Merry on 11.514)

515.n: τὸ ὃν μένος 'that might of his' (Merry on 11.515)
possessive ὅς (= ἑόν), not the relative
used as a noun; dative with εἴκων

515.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

516.n: 'battle, the fray' (δήϊος 'hostile'); ἐν αἰνῇ δηιοτῆτι as Iliad 3.20

517.n: with the subjunctives μυθήσομαι and ὀνομήνω
short-vowel subjunctive (= μυθήσωμαι), parallel to ὀνομήνω; the half-line as 4.240, Iliad 2.488
aorist subjunctive with ἄν: 'I could not name'

518.n: epic ὅσσος = ὅσος, with λαόν: 'how great a host', taking up πάντας (517)

518.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

519.n: exclamatory, with τὸν Τηλεφίδην: '(I will tell) what a man he slew', as ἀλλʼ οἷον τόδʼ ἔρεξε 4.242
patronymic of Eurypylus (520); only here in Homer
aorist middle, active in sense, of κατεναίρω 'slay', compound of ἐναίρω (ἐνήρατο Iliad 5.43); only here in Homer

520.n: son of Telephus, king of the Mysians, and of Astyoche, Priam's sister or daughter; the last ally to come to the Trojans, his mother won over by Priam's gift of a golden vine (Merry on 11.520)

521.n: a Mysian people of Teuthrania, named, it is said, from the river Ceteius; Strabo (13, p. 615) owned he did not know who they were; Aristarchus took the word as 'great men' (κῆτος), others read κήδειοι 'kinsmen' or χήτειοι (scholia); some in Merry's day saw in them the Hittites (Merry on 11.521 and critical note); only here in Homer
'of a woman': gifts given to a woman, Priam's golden vine for Eurypylus' mother; the phrase again 15.247, of Eriphyle (Merry on 11.521, 11.520); in Homer only these two places

522.n: son of Dawn and king of the Ethiopians, who killed Antilochus (4.187–188); named in Homer only here

523.n: the builder of the horse, as 8.493

524.n: οἱ ἄριστοι 'the chiefs', in apposition to the subject of κατεβαίνομεν (523)
in tmesis with τέταλτο (ἐπιτέλλω 'lay upon, entrust')
in tmesis: ἐπὶ … τέταλτο, unaugmented (= ἐπετέταλτο), as ἐπὶ … ἐτέταλτο Iliad 2.643; singular verb with neuter plural subject

525.n: ἠμέν … ἠδέ 'both … and'; the line, after Iliad 5.751 (ἀνακλῖναι πυκινὸν νέφος), was not known to Aristarchus, though all manuscripts have it; Merry brackets it (Merry on 11.525 and critical note)
'lean back', i.e. open (the door of the horse); infinitive explaining πάντα (524)
the hollow horse with the men hidden in it, as 4.277; words that suit a cloud are forced with λόχος (Merry on 11.525)

526.n: = ἔνθα, opening the main clause after ὅτʼ (523)
Δαναῶν ἡγήτορες ἠδὲ μέδοντες as Iliad 11.816
participle of μέδω 'rule', used as a noun

527.n: unaugmented (= ἔτρεμον); plural verb with the neuter plural γυῖα
adverbial 'beneath (him)', or in tmesis with τρέμον (ὑποτρέμω), as Iliad 10.390

528.n: οὔ ποτε 'never'; accent from enclitic ποτε

529.n: = οὔτε; οὔτε … οὔτε 'neither … nor', after οὔ ποτε (528)

529.p: verb · aor. part. act. acc. sg. masc.
529.n: 'turn pale' (ὦχρος 'paleness', Iliad 3.35); only here in Homer
epic acc. χρόα (Attic χρῶτα); accusative of respect

530.p: verb · aor. part. mid. acc. sg. masc.

530.n: 'beg as a suppliant'; με understood; + inf.

531.n: ἵππος with the suffix -θεν 'from', printed as one word, as 8.515
epic aorist infinitive of ἐξίημι 'let out' (= ἐξεῖναι), which suits ἱκέτευεν better than the variant ἐξίμεναι, from ἔξειμι 'go out' (Merry on 11.531 and critical note)

532.n: 'weighted with bronze', as ἰὸς χαλκοβαρής Iliad 15.465

533.n: epic gen. -οιο; Πριάμοιο πόλιν διεπέρσαμεν αἰπήν as 3.130
epic fem. αἰπήν, as from αἰπός (= αἰπεῖαν)

534.n: 'his share of the spoil', as ἴση μοῖρα Iliad 9.318 (Merry on 11.534)
a special prize of honor: in the Little Iliad of Lesches it is Andromache, but any choice piece of the spoil may be meant (Merry on 11.534)

534.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

535.p: verb · pf. part. mid./pass. nom. sg. masc.

536.n: adverbial accusative: 'at close quarters' (cf. αὐτοσχεδόν), a feminine form like ἀμφαδίην (Merry on 11.536)

536.p: verb · pf. part. mid./pass. nom. sg. masc.
536.n: 'stabbed', of a thrust at close range, against βεβλημένος (535) of a missile
οἷά τε 'such things as', subject of γίγνεται (537); second accent from enclitic τε

537.n: singular verb with the neuter plural οἷα (536)
'indiscriminately': the war god rages against all alike, as ξυνὸς Ἐνυάλιος Iliad 18.309 (Merry on 11.537)

539.n: unaugmented, contracted (= ἐφοίτα); the lemma of a scholion gives ᾤχετο (Merry's critical note on 11.539)
adverbial: μακρὰ βιβᾶσα 'with long strides', as μακρὰ βιβάς Iliad 7.213

539.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. fem.
539.n: epic athematic present βίβημι 'stride'; feminine with ψυχή (538)

'of asphodel', oxytone as an adjective; the asphodel, a plant with a tall stalk and pale flowers, is still planted on graves in the Greek islands, perhaps as simple food for the dead (Merry on 11.539); a scholion doubts whether to read κατὰ σφοδελόν (Merry's critical note); again 573, 24.13

540.n: 'glad', with ψυχή; γηθοσύνη ὅ 'glad that' (Merry on 11.540); Aristophanes and Herodian seem to have read the noun γηθοσύνῃ 'for joy', as Iliad 21.390, and so a few manuscripts (Merry's critical note on 11.540)
neuter relative ὅ used as ὅτι 'that, because'

541.p: verb · pf. part. act. gen. pl. masc.
541.n: epic perfect participle (Attic κατατεθνεώτων); νεκύων κατατεθνηώτων as 37, 10.530; again 564

542.p: verb · pres. part. mid. nom. pl. fem.

542.n: epic εἴρομαι = ἔρομαι: they asked about their cares, those dear to them above, as Bothe takes it, and not 'told their cares', as a scholion has it (Merry on 11.542)
in apposition to the subject of εἴροντο

544.p: verb · pf. part. mid./pass. nom. sg. fem.

544.n: the award of Achilles' arms, a story of the Cyclic epics: in the Aethiopis the Trojan captives judged that Odysseus had done them more harm, and Ajax fell on his sword (Merry on 11.543)

545.n: article used as relative; cognate accusative with νίκησα: τὴν (νίκην) νίκησα, as βουλὰς βουλεύειν 6.61 (Merry on 11.545); accent from enclitic μιν

545.p: verb · pres. part. mid. nom. sg. masc.
545.n: middle 'go to law, plead one's case', as 12.440 (Merry on 11.545)

546.n: = ἀμφί, placed after its noun: 'about, for'
epic gen. -ῆος; single λ for the meter

546.g: had set it as a prize
546.n: 'set up as a prize', as θῆκε Iliad 23.263 (Merry on 11.546)

547.n: Aristarchus rejected the line (Merry's critical note on 11.547); Nitzsch objects that Trojan captives are unlikely judges, that Homer would say κοῦροι or υἷες, not παῖδες Τρώων, and that Odysseus would hardly make Athena the author of the award (Merry on 11.547)

548.n: ὡς … ὄφελον + inf.: 'would that …', a wish that can no longer come true
= ἐπί: 'for (the sake of)', as δώρῳ ἔπι μεγάλῳ Iliad 10.304 (Merry on 11.548)
'prize', not ἄεθλος 'contest': ἕνεκʼ αὐτῶν (549) shows that the arms are meant (Merry on 11.548)

550.n: = Αἴαντα, elided and aspirated before ὅς; in apposition to κεφαλήν (549); 550–551 = Iliad 17.279–280, with the nominative
'beyond (the others)', τῶν ἄλλων Δαναῶν (551), repeated with each accusative, as 1.66 (Merry on 11.550); accent thrown back
unaugmented pluperfect: 'had been made', i.e. was

552.n: epic dat. pl. -οισι(ν); ἐπέεσσι … μειλιχίοισιν 'with gentle words', as Iliad 4.256

553.n: = ἄρα: 'after all, as it seems', of a surprise
+ fut. inf. λήσεσθαι (554): 'were you not, after all, to …'

554.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

554.n: dative of the person: 'your anger at me'

555.n: emphatic: it was the gods who set the arms as a prize, so your anger should not fall on me (Merry on 11.555)

556.n: epic σφι(ν) = αὐτοῖς; dative of disadvantage: 'lost to them'
of a man as a stronghold, as in Psalm 144.2 (Merry on 11.555)
uncontracted -εο (= ἀπώλου): 'you perished'; Apollonius' Lexicon has ἀπώλετο (Merry's critical note on 11.556)
epic σεῖο = σοῦ; genitive of cause with ἀχνύμεθα (558) (Merry on 11.556)

558.p: verb · aor. part. mid. gen. sg. masc.
558.n: athematic aorist middle (ἐφθίμην) of φθίω, by-form of φθίνω: 'perished'; agrees with σεῖο (556); epic gen. -οιο

559.n: predicate, ἐστί understood; οὐ … αἴτιος ἄλλος, ἀλλά as 8.311–312 (Merry on 11.559)
the logical form would be 'but Zeus is to blame, who hated …' (Merry on 11.559)

560.n: in tmesis with ἔθηκεν (ἐπιτίθημι 'lay upon'); cf. οἷσιν ἐπὶ Ζεὺς θῆκε κακὸν μόρον Iliad 6.357 (Merry on 11.559)

562.n: plural possessive for the speaker alone; with μῦθον (561)
'manly, proud' (ἄγαν + ἀνήρ), as θυμὸς ἀγήνωρ Iliad 9.635

564.p: verb · pf. part. act. gen. pl. masc.

565.n: = κε, aspirated before the rough breathing of ὅμως; with προσέφη: what would have happened

'nevertheless', in Homer again only Iliad 12.393, which Merry compares; the usual word is ἔμπης; most copies accented ὁμῶς 'alike' (scholia); the word and the loose κεχολωμένος make Merry suspect 565–567 as the start of the later passage 568–627 (Merry on 11.565 and critical note)

565.p: verb · pf. part. mid./pass. nom. sg. masc.

566.n: epic dat. pl. -οισι; φίλος 'one's own'; θυμὸς ἐνὶ στήθεσσι φίλοισι as Iliad 13.73

567.p: verb · pf. part. act. gen. pl. masc.
567.n: epic perfect participle, used here without νεκύων, which Merry finds strange (Merry on 11.565)

568.n: = ἔνθα; a scholion marks 568–627 as spurious; Merry takes the whole passage from 565 for an early, perhaps Attic, addition, in which Odysseus sees into the depths of Erebus (Merry on 11.565 and critical note on 11.568)
son of Zeus, king in Crete (Iliad 13.450, Odyssey 19.178–179); not the judge of the dead of later legend, but lawgiver, king and judge among the shades as he was in life (Merry on 11.568)

569.p: verb · pres. part. act. acc. sg. masc.
verb · pres. part. act. acc. sg. masc.
569.n: 'give judgments' (θέμιστες); with the dative here, with the genitive at 9.114 (Merry on 11.569)

570.p: verb · pres. part. mid. acc. sg. masc.

570.n: with ἄνακτα in apposition: 'him, the king' (Merry on 11.569)
'their rights': they asked him about their cases, as Damm takes it, rather than 'stated their cases' (Merry on 11.570)

571.p: verb · pres. part. mid. nom. pl. masc.
571.n: some sitting as they wait their turn, others standing as each states his case (Merry on 11.569)

571.p: verb · pf. part. act. nom. pl. masc.
571.n: epic pf. part. ἑσταώς (= ἑστώς); second accent from enclitic τε
an irregular form for εὐρύπυλον; εὐρυπυλὲς Ἄϊδος δῶ as Iliad 23.74

572.n: Minos; governed by μετά, which follows
the giant hunter, still at his hunting among the dead, driving phantom beasts, the shadows of those he once hunted (Merry on 11.572); the constellation at 5.274

573.p: verb · pres. part. act. acc. sg. masc.
573.n: epic present εἰλέω, contracted -εῦντα (= εἰλέοντα): 'drive together into a herd' (Merry on 11.573)

574.n: the man in life, against the phantoms he now drives (Merry on 11.572)

575.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

576.n: the giant, son of Earth (7.324); the name perhaps from a root 'swell' (Merry on 11.576)
aorist εἶδον serves as aorist of ὁράω
Earth personified, his mother (Γαιήιον υἱόν 7.324); Ionic gen. -ης

577.p: verb · pres. part. mid. acc. sg. masc.

577.n: a measure of land, later 100 Greek feet in length, 10,000 square feet in area; Merry suggests 'roods' (Merry on 11.577); the fallen Ares covers seven, Iliad 21.407

578.n: the whole, with the part ἧπαρ: a double accusative

578.p: verb · pres. part. mid. nom. du. masc.

578.n: 'cut, tear'; plural verb with the dual subject

579.n: the membrane enclosing the bowels (δέρω 'flay'), Latin omentum; an ancient alternative, 'the vulture's beak', would make δύνοντες 'plunging' (Merry on 11.579); only here in Homer

579.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. pl. masc.
579.n: present of the by-form δύνω, + acc.: 'entering'; plural with the dual γῦπε (578)
unaugmented (= ἀπημύνετο); middle 'ward off from oneself'

580.n: mother of Apollo and Artemis; for the outrage Tityus was slain by Artemis (Pindar), with Apollo (Pausanias), or by Zeus (Hyginus) (Merry on 11.581)
aorist of ἑλκέω, epic by-form of ἕλκω: 'laid violent hands on'; unaugmented; the manuscripts vary (ἤλκησε, εἵλκυσε and others), and La Roche takes ἕλκησε for Aristarchus' reading (Merry on 11.580)
'glorious' (κῦδος); Διὸς κυδρὴ παράκοιτις is Hera's title at Iliad 18.184, and strange of Leto (Merry on 11.581)

581.n: = Πυθώδε, Πυθώ (Delphi, 8.80) with the suffix -δε 'to', printed as one word

581.p: verb · pres. part. mid. acc. sg. fem.

581.n: 'with fair dancing floors' (καλός + χορός); only here in Homer
epic gen. -ῆος; a town near the Cephissus on the borders of Boeotia, called Phanoteus in Strabo's day (Merry on 11.581); among the Phocian towns at Iliad 2.520

582.n: Plato connects the name with τάλας 'wretched', Merry rather with τλῆναι 'dare'; his offense is told in several ways (Merry on 11.582); only here in Homer

582.p: verb · pres. part. act. acc. sg. masc.

583.p: verb · pf. part. act. acc. sg. masc.

584.n: unaugmented; στεῦμαι, elsewhere 'declare, pledge', here of eager striving, 'was set (on drinking)', a state of mind as Aristarchus explained it, or an eager gesture; never 'stood' in Homer (Merry on 11.584)

584.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. masc.
584.n: epic diectasis (= διψῶν): 'thirsting'; only here in Homer
epic uncontracted aor. inf. (= πιεῖν); with ἑλέσθαι: 'take (something) to drink'

585.n: epic ὁσσάκι = ὁσάκις; answered by τοσσάχʼ (586); + optative of repeated action
= κύψειε, the 'Aeolic' optative in -ειε; optative of repeated action

585.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

586.n: = τοσσάκι, elided and aspirated before ὕδωρ; epic τοσσάκι = τοσάκις, answering ὁσσάκι (585)
= ἀπολέσκετο, iter. (-σκ-) of the aorist middle ἀπωλόμην: 'would vanish'; only here in Homer

586.p: verb · aor. part. pass. nom. sg. neut.
586.n: 'swallowed up', in form a 2nd aorist participle; the active compounds ἀναβρόξειε 12.240, καταβρόξειε 4.222 (Merry on 11.586); variants ἀναβροχθέν, ἀναβρυχέν (Eustathius, in Merry's critical note); only here in Homer

587.n: iter. (-σκ-), unaugmented: 'would appear', as Iliad 11.64; formed from an aorist stem, the passive ἐφάνην or, as others hold, an active ἔφανον (Merry on 11.587)
iter. (-σκ-) of an aorist κατέζηνα, from a present καταζαίνω 'dry up' (cf. ἀζαίνω) (Merry on 11.587); only here in Homer

588.n: epic δένδρεον = δένδρον; neuter plural with the singular χέε
with κρῆθεν: 'down from the head', as Iliad 16.548

'from the head' (cf. κάρη, κρήδεμνον): κατὰ κρῆθεν, Aristarchus' reading, 'down over his head', as the scholion explains it (κατὰ κεφαλῆς); Bekker's second edition reads κατʼ ἄκρηθεν (Merry on 11.588 and critical note)

589.n: 'pear tree'; in apposition to δένδρεα (588); 589–590 = 7.115–116, the orchard of Alcinous
'pomegranate tree'; in Homer only here and 7.115
'with splendid fruit' (ἀγλαός + καρπός); two-termination adjective; in Homer only here and 7.115

590.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. pl. fem.

591.n: the trees; genitive with ἐπὶ … μάσασθαι
= ὁπότε, with the optative of repeated action
= ἰθύσειε, 'Aeolic' optative in -ειε: 'press straight on', + inf.
in tmesis with μάσασθαι (ἐπιμαίομαι 'grasp at'), as ἐπεμαίετο 531; or with χερσί, 'with his hands'
in tmesis: ἐπὶ … μάσασθαι = ἐπιμάσασθαι 'grasp at', + gen. τῶν

592.n: = δέ, opening the main clause after ὁπότʼ (591)
iter. (-σκ-), unaugmented, with -α- for -ε-; the same form at 8.374, to which Merry refers (Merry on 11.592)
uncontracted (Attic νέφη); ποτὶ νέφεα σκιόεντα as 8.374

593.n: son of Aeolus, at Ephyre, 'the craftiest of men' (Iliad 6.153–154); Curtius takes the name for a reduplicated form of σοφός (Merry on 11.593)

593.p: verb · pres. part. act. acc. sg. masc.

594.p: verb · pres. part. act. acc. sg. masc.

595.n: ἦ τοι (= ἤτοι) with μέν, answered by ἀλλʼ ὅτε (596)

595.p: verb · pres. part. mid. nom. sg. masc.
595.n: 'prop oneself, lean' (cf. σκῆπτρον); in Homer here and 17.196

596.n: the clashing vowels of λᾶαν ἄνω ὤθεσκε paint the labor of the push, as Eustathius observes (Merry on 11.596)
with the optative of repeated action
the subject is Sisyphus, with ὑπερβαλέειν transitive (Merry on 11.596), or the stone ('was about to go over')

597.n: iter. (-σκ-) of the aorist, unaugmented; the form as Iliad 22.197

'mighty force' (κραταιός): the force within the stone, its weight, as a scholion explains it (ἡ κραταιὰ δύναμις, ὅ ἐστι τὸ βάρος), or a 'Mighty One' outside it, like δαίμων (587); Aristarchus took it for an adverb, 'mightily', and Ptolemy of Ascalon divided it into two words, both unlikely to Merry; a Κραταιΐς is Scylla's mother at 12.124 (Merry on 11.597); only here as a common noun

598.n: Aristotle quotes the line with ἐπὶ δάπεδόνδε for ἔπειτα πέδονδε (Rhetoric 1411b34–35), as a metaphor that gives life to lifeless things (Merry on 11.597 and critical note on 11.598)
πέδον with the suffix -δε 'to', printed as one word (the Iliad prints πέδον δέ, 13.796)
unaugmented (= ἐκυλίνδετο); free of hiatus, the line runs as easily as the falling stone (Eustathius, in Merry on 11.596)
'ruthless', as if the stone had a will, as Iliad 4.521; the original of Virgil's improbus (Merry on 11.597)

599.n: iter. (-σκ-) of the aorist ὦσα, formed from the aorist stem (Merry on 11.587)

599.p: verb · pres. part. mid. nom. sg. masc.

600.n: in tmesis: κατὰ … ἔρρεεν = κατέρρεεν; uncontracted (Attic ἔρρει); ρ doubled after the augment
gen. of κάρη (stem κρατ-): as he thrusts the stone his head is bent low, so the dust from his feet and the stone seems to rise from it (Merry on 11.600)
pluperfect of ὄρνυμι with imperfect sense: 'arose'

601.n: Sisyphus; governed by μετά, which follows

Ionic βίη = βία: βίην Ἡρακληείην 'the might of Heracles', i.e. mighty Heracles; unlike Minos and the others, he knows Odysseus, speaks to him and goes back into the house of Hades, like Achilles and Ajax (Merry on 11.601)

602.n: in apposition to βίην Ἡρακληείην; 602–604 were rejected in antiquity, said by the scholia to be the work of Onomacritus; Merry keeps the Heracles scene but rejects these three lines, which divide the man into phantom, body and soul and assume his deification and marriage to Hebe, unknown to Homer (cf. Iliad 18.117) (Merry on 11.601 and critical note on 11.602)
the man himself, as against his εἴδωλον

603.n: the goddess Youth, who pours nectar for the gods (Iliad 4.2–3), a maiden in Homer, as the scholia object (Merry on 11.601); some took the word for his own youth, ἥβη (scholia, in Merry's critical note on 11.602)

604.n: in apposition to Ἥβην; the line = Hesiod, Theogony 952, and a scholion calls it an insertion of Onomacritus (Merry's critical note on 11.602); Merry brackets it
'golden-sandaled' (χρυσός + πέδιλον); two-termination adjective; only here in Homer

605.n: postpositive ὡς 'like', accented after its noun

606.p: verb · pres. part. mid. gen. pl. masc.
606.n: 'flying scared', as of runaway horses, Iliad 6.38 (Merry on 11.606); with νεκύων (605)

606.p: verb · pf. part. act. nom. sg. masc.
606.n: perfect with present sense, + dat.: of a stern, lowering look, as of Apollo in wrath, Iliad 1.47 (Merry on 11.606)

607.n: 'uncased', out of its case (γωρυτός, 21.54) (Merry on 11.607); predicative

607.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

607.n: epic -φι(ν) ending, here dative with ἐπί (elsewhere genitive with ἀπό, Iliad 8.300)

608.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. masc.
608.n: 'peer about', a look of anxious watchfulness; four participles with no finite verb, perhaps a deliberate abruptness (Merry on 11.608)
with βαλέοντι: 'ever as if about to shoot' (Merry on 11.608)

608.p: verb · fut. part. act. dat. sg. masc.
608.n: epic future βαλέω (= βαλῶ), uncontracted; dative with ἐοικώς

608.p: verb · pf. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

609.n: predicate, placed first for emphasis (Merry on 11.613)
ἀμφὶ περί 'round about': the two can hardly be told apart, and need not be written as one word, as Bekker wrote them (Merry on 11.609)
the 'carrier' (cf. ἀείρω), like τελαμών (610), which is here the more specific word (Merry on 11.609)

610.n: predicate: the baldric was a golden strap
unaugmented pluperfect; singular with the neuter plural subject

611.n: 'bear', usually feminine; in Homer the animal only here (the constellation, Ἄρκτος, 5.273)
= τε; τε … τε … τε 'both … and … and'
'bright-eyed, fierce-eyed'; commonly referred to χαρά, better to a root 'glow, sparkle' (Merry on 11.611); one manuscript has χαλεποί (Merry's critical note); only here in Homer

612.n: Ionic -ίη; μάχαι τʼ ἀνδροκτασίαι τε as Iliad 24.548

613.n: with the participle, which stands for a wish of its own: 'would he had never made it; but having made it, may he make nothing else like it', as 4.684 (Merry on 11.613)

613.p: verb · aor. part. mid. nom. sg. masc.

613.n: = μηδέ; μή … μηδέ as in Herodotus 8.144 (Nitzsch, in Merry on 11.613)
optative of wish: either praise, since no later work could match it, or, as Merry prefers, dread at the terrible images (Merry on 11.613)

614.n: unaugmented (= ἐγκατέθετο), with apocopated κατ- (= κατα-): 'stored up in his craft', i.e. in his inventive mind, as ἑῷ ἐγκάτθετο θυμῷ 23.223 (Merry on 11.613); a scholion's reading ὃς κείνῳ τελαμῶνι ἑὴν ἐγκάτθετο τέχνην, 'who put all his art into that strap' (Merry's critical note on 11.614)

616.n: accent from enclitic μʼ; the line = 10.265

616.p: verb · pres. part. mid. nom. sg. masc.

618.n: set before its noun, with emphasis: 'an evil sort of fate' (Merry on 11.618)
'lead, carry on' (cf. ἡγέομαι), like ἄγειν, διάγειν 'pass (a life)' in later Greek (Merry on 11.618); in Homer here and 17.217

619.n: iter. (-σκ-), uncontracted, unaugmented: 'used to bear, endure'; only here in Homer
epic ἠέλιος = ἥλιος; gen. -οιο; ὑπʼ αὐγὰς ἠελίοιο as 498

621.n: comparative of κακός: Eurystheus, son of Sthenelus, to whom Heracles was bound through Hera's spite (Iliad 19.97–133) (Merry on 11.621)

622.n: perfect stem δεδμη- (cf. δάμνημι): 'I had been made subject'; after this line one Venetian manuscript adds two mutilated lines naming Eurystheus, restored by Cobet (Merry's critical note on 11.622)
the labors of Heracles, as Iliad 8.363

623.n: = κύνα; Homer does not name the dog, Cerberus first in Hesiod (Theogony 311), but Iliad 8.368 shows the story known in a simple form (Merry on 11.623)

623.p: verb · fut. part. act. acc. sg. masc.
623.n: = ἄξοντα; future participle of purpose, as ἄξοντα κύνα Iliad 8.368

624.n: genitive of comparison: than this labor; second accent from enclitic γε; good manuscripts read τοῦδέ τι, others τοῦδʼ ἔτι (Merry's critical note on 11.624)

625.n: aorist ἤνεικα (stem ἐνεικ-) of φέρω, compounded: 'carried up'

626.n: 'escorted, conducted', as 6.255 (Merry on 11.626); singular verb with two subjects

627.n: end of the passage a scholion marks as spurious from 568 (Merry's critical note on 11.568)

627.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

628.n: εἰ + optative, of a hope: 'in case'; accent from enclitic τις

630.n: = κε, with the aorist indicative ἴδον: what might have been
with ἴδον, as ἔτʼ ἔλθοι (628) (Merry on 11.630)
unaugmented (= ἤθελον); second accent from enclitic περ

631.n: Hereas of Megara said that Peisistratus put the line into the Nekyia to please the Athenians (Plutarch, Theseus 20, in Merry's critical note on 11.631); Merry brackets it
son of Zeus (Iliad 14.317–318); second accent from enclitic τε

632.n: in tmesis with ἀγείρετο (ἐπαγείρω 'gather together'): 'up gathered' (Merry on 11.632)
= ἔθνεα, uncontracted (Attic ἔθνη); ἔθνεα νεκρῶν as 34
in tmesis: ἐπὶ … ἀγείρετο, unaugmented; middle 'gather'; singular with the neuter plural subject

633.n: dative of manner, as θεσπεσίῃ ἰαχῇ 43
'green-pale': fear that turns men pale; χλωρὸν δέος ᾕρει as 43, Iliad 7.479

634.n: 'lest', with the optative πέμψειεν (635) after a past tense
adjective from Γοργώ, the Gorgon: 'the Gorgon's head', as Iliad 5.741; Merry takes it of any horrible spectre, 'a Gorgon-head of some terrible monster' (Merry on 11.632)
in apposition to the Gorgon implied in Γοργείην, as κυνώπιδος after ἐμός Iliad 3.180 (Merry on 11.632)

635.n: Ionic gen. -εω, one syllable by synizesis
'Aeolic' optative in -ειε, after μή in past sequence

636.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

637.n: in tmesis with λῦσαι (ἀναλύω 'loose'); acute before enclitic τε
mooring cables from stern to shore

639.n: κῦμα ῥόοιο 'the swell of the current', the current down the Ocean-stream carrying them back toward the sea (Merry on 11.639)

640.n: instrumental dative, the reading Eustathius found in the old copies; Merry prefers the nominative εἰρεσίη, parallel to οὖρος: no wind blew in that unearthly place, so they rowed until they came into the ordinary world (Merry on 11.640 and critical note)
'fair wind' (not οὖρος 'guardian'); a verb such as ἦν or φέρε understood
